blocks.title: Give the agent whatever the page actually is
blocks.description: Scrape a page as Markdown and, when you need it, as HTML, links, screenshots, images, video and audio URLs, a summary or schema-shaped JSON. Crawl a section, map a site, search, read a PDF or Word file, drive a live browser session, or let the browsing agent answer a question across pages — all through the Firecrawl API, with every crawl animated in a spider console. Works without a key at a lower rate limit.

showcase.user_prompt: Crawl the Astravia plugin docs under /docs/plugin and tell me what I need to declare for an activity tab.
showcase.assistant_reply: Crawled 9 pages under /docs/plugin (12-page limit, depth 2, sitemap seeded). The tab contract is in ui-slots.md: a plugin registers a component with zero props, declares scope_use, and must keep its UI inside the panel rectangle — no fixed positioning or portals. Two /blog links fell outside the include rule, so the run stopped at 9 pages rather than the full site.

items.title: Thirteen tools, one contract
items.description: scrape, batch_scrape, crawl, map, search, extract, parse, video, interact, agent, index_search, job_status and monitor. Each maps onto a Firecrawl v2 endpoint, so the plugin's answers match what the API actually returned.

items.title: Pages that need JavaScript
items.description: Rendering happens upstream, so an app shell still arrives as readable text. Wait for a selector, click through a tab, or screenshot the result without wiring a browser yourself.

items.title: Documents, not just HTML
items.description: PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX go through the parse endpoint with OCR, so scanned pages and spreadsheets come back as Markdown instead of being refused as binary. HTML, JSON and layout blocks are available when the prose is not the point.

items.title: A browser that stays open
items.description: When a page needs a login or ten clicks before it is readable, interact opens a session in Firecrawl's sandbox and runs Node, Python or Bash inside it. State survives between calls, and the browser is closed when you stop the session.

items.title: Answers that span pages
items.description: The agent mode browses on its own when you cannot name the URL, bounded by a credit budget. A run that hits the budget returns a partial answer that is labelled as partial.

items.title: Curated indexes
items.description: Search developer docs, issues and pull requests, government sites, or academic papers — and walk a paper's citations — without falling back to a general web search.

items.title: Media URLs you can hand over
items.description: Ask a page for its video and audio and you get the signed links Firecrawl found, including HLS/DASH manifests. They expire after about an hour, so the answer says so.

items.title: Honest about what failed
items.description: Denied and failed pages are read back from the crawl's errors endpoint and counted separately, so a short crawl is explained rather than quietly truncated.

items.title: Spider console
items.description: The start page sits in the middle and each hop moves outward one ring. Spiders drop onto the page being fetched, packets travel down the active spokes, and refused pages stay visible as dashed threads.

blocks.content:
## One connection, keyless to start

The crawler console has a single connection bar:

- **Endpoint** — empty means `https://api.firecrawl.dev`. A self-hosted instance is `http://localhost:3002`.
- **API key** — stored in the host credential vault, never in a settings file, a log or a tool argument. Leave it empty to run on the keyless tier at a lower rate limit.
- **Credits and limits** are reported verbatim: out of credits, a wrong key and a rate limit each read differently.
- **Outputs per page** — Markdown is always kept; tick links, images, video and audio, summaries, HTML, JSON or change tracking when the run needs them.

Firecrawl also publishes an MCP server and a CLI. This plugin embeds neither: MCP would expose every tool a second time under `mcp_` names, route calls around the console and the run history, and leave the sign-in in the host's MCP settings where the plugin cannot read or revoke it; the CLI is a second client for the same endpoints. The API is the one path that keeps your key in the vault and the whole tool surface in one place.

## Reading the spider web

- **Center dot** — the page you started from; each ring outward is one link hop.
- **Solid dot** — page fetched and converted. **Hollow dashed dot** — page refused; the console names the reason.
- **Spider with a pulse ring** — being fetched right now; the moving packet is the request travelling down that spoke.
- **Red ×** — the request failed upstream (timeout, HTTP error, refused page).

Animation only runs while the tab is visible and the crawl is live, and it is disabled automatically when your system asks for reduced motion.

items.title: Install and enable the plugin
items.description: The Crawler tab appears in the activity panel, and the agent gains the firecrawl tools plus the skill. It works immediately, without a key.

items.title: Paste a URL and crawl
items.description: Defaults are 25 pages and depth 2. Widen them only if you need more; the console lists every refused or failed page.

items.title: Optional: connect your own Firecrawl account
items.description: Open the account card above, click Authorize to sign in and create a key on firecrawl.dev, then paste it back — it is verified against the billing endpoint before it is saved. A self-hosted endpoint goes in the console's connection bar.

items.title: Or just ask
items.description: “Crawl example.com/docs and summarize the API pages”, “read this PDF as Markdown”, “where is the video on this page”. The agent picks the tool and the same console follows along.

blocks.content: Pages are fetched and converted on Firecrawl's servers, not on your machine — the URL and any local file you parse leave your device. Signed media links expire after about an hour. DRM-protected streams are reported, never decrypted; robots.txt is honoured by default; logins and captchas are not defeated.
